question.leadin: This leader was called the "Hero of Two Worlds" for his involvement in both European and South American conflicts.
question.text: Name this general, who led the Redshirts in Expedition of the Thousand to defeat the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies.
question.clue: This man married a woman named Anita, whom he met while fighting in civil wars in Brazil and Uruguay.

swap.leadin: This family included such scions as Lorenzo the Magnificent, who was targeted by the Pazzi [Pot-see]conspiracy.
swap.text: Name this powerful Italian family. Niccolo Machiavelli [Mah-kee-ah-vell-ee] dedicated The Prince to a member of this family, and women from this family named Maria and Catherine became queen regents of France.
swap.clue: One member of this group excommunicated Martin Luther.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about Italy during World War II.
question.text: A member of the House of Savoy, this man saw the rise and fall of Mussolini during his reign as King of Italy.
question.clue: This King of Italy handed power to Mussolini following the March on Rome, and declared an armistice with the Allies in 1943; following the war, he abdicated the throne to his son.

swap.leadin: Colonial expansion by Europeans began long before 1492. name the locations of some Greek colonies.
swap.text: In an attempt to inhabit Magna Graecia [MAG-na GREE-see-ah], located in modern Southern Italy, Syracuse was founded on this island in the Mediterranean Sea.
swap.clue: Mamertines who moved to this island helped cause the First Punic War by asking Rome for aid.

question.leadin: The French won a victory at Agnadello while acting as a member of this alliance.
question.text: Name this alliance named for a city in France, formed by France, Aragon, the Holy Roman Empire, and the Papacy against the aggression of a certain Italian city.
question.clue: Its opponent blamed the defeat on the indecisive leadership of Leonardo Loredan, which was thought to have contributed to the loss at Agnadello.

swap.leadin: In this book, the author concludes that "men forget more easily the death of their father than the loss of their patrimony."
swap.text: Name this political treatise which also claims "it is far safer to be feared than loved." It is the most famous work of Niccolo Machiavelli.
swap.clue: This book, which distinguishes between hereditary and ecclesiastical principalities, was a follow-up to its author's earlier Discourses on Livy, which described the ideal republic.

question.text: One of Cesare Borgia's most infamous acts was this debauched party. Cesare invited fifty prostitutes to this event, which was named for the items strewn on the ground for the courtesans to pick up.
question.answerHtml: Banquet of the Chestnuts (or Ballet of the Chestnuts)
question.clue: This hedonistic party held in the Apostolic Palace in 1501. This famed orgy was named for the objects that "fifty honest prostitutes" attempted to pick up off the floor while crawling between flaming candles.

swap.text: This "Great" king founded the Ostrogothic kingdom of Italy. He supposedly killed Odoacer, the man who overthrew the last Western Roman Emperor, with his bare hands.
swap.clue: He won the original Battle of the Isonzo, which led to an amusing banquet in which he toasted - and then personally strangled - the man who had deposed Romulus Augustulus.

question.leadin: In honor of this family, the architect Filarete designed an ideal city in the shape of an eight-point star.
question.text: Name this family. A member of this family, Francesco, became duke of a city previously ruled by the Viscontis.
question.clue: Prominent members included one who was briefly exiled after trying to displace Bona of Savoy; the cardinal Ascanio; and someone who married the daughter of the duke of Ferrara, Beatrice d'Este, in 1491.

swap.leadin: Answer the follow about capitals of the Roman Empire which are not Rome.
swap.text: This city became the capital of the Ostrogothic Kingdom after Odoacer overthrew the last Western Roman Emperor, Romulus Augustulus.
swap.clue: It became the seat of the Byzantine governor of Italy in the sixth century, and its namesake Cosmography was written around 700.

question.text: The League of Cambrai was formed to combat this "Most Serene" Italian republic, which was ruled by "doges." During the Fourth Crusade, Enrico Dandolo, the ruler of this republic, sent crusaders off to siege Constantinople.
question.clue: Enrico Dandolo of this polity successfully diverted the 4th Crusade to sack Constantinople, and ships supplied by this polity won a decisive victory at the Battle of Lepanto.

swap.leadin: This group kidnapped U.S. General James Dozier.
swap.text: "Name this leftist group best known for abducting and then killing former Christian Democratic prime minister Aldo Moro in 1978. This group was very active during the "years of lead".
swap.clue: It's not a political party, but a "Front of Firmness" opposing this group was maintained by ideological allies of it who had accepted the Historic Compromise, such as Enrico Berlinguer.

question.text: After Theodoric's death, power in the Ostrogothic kingdom was controlled by this daughter of his, first as regent and then as queen. Justinian used her murder as pretext for invading Italy.
question.clue: When her son Atalaric was dying, she began planning to surrender the kingdom to the Byzantine Empire in an attempt to secure her position.

swap.leadin: Vannozza dei Cattanei was the mother to four members of this family.
swap.text: Identify this Renaissance-era family whose members included Cesare, Lucrezia, and their depraved father, Pope Alexander VI.
swap.clue: A Patriarch of this family ordered the likely fictional Banquet of the Chestnuts, a debauched party in the papal palace.

question.text: Muhammad al-Idrisi created a map known as the Tabula Rogeriana for Roger II, a king of this island. A Norman knigdom on this non-Britain island controlled Apulia and Calabria before it passed to the Angevins.
question.clue: For four years, this polity was ruled by Tancred of Lecce, who launched an unsuccessful rebellion against the emperor Henry VI and was its last Norman ruler.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Africans in Renaissance Italy.
swap.text: John Brackett argued that this man's heir Alessandro was the son of the African servant Simonetta. This dedicatee of Machiavelli's The Prince married his daughter Catherine to King Henry II of France.
swap.answerHtml: Lorenzo II de’ Medici [reject “Lorenzo” or “Lorenzo de’ Medici”]

question.leadin: Answer the following about food and cooking during the Italian Renaissance.
question.text: This humanist scholar's diet book De vita uses the doctrine of signature to argue for eating foods based on their appearances, suggesting eating walnuts since they look like the brain. This scholar founded the Florentine Academy in an attempt to revive Platonic thought.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about possible defenestrations which didn't happen in Prague.
swap.text: This 1478 plot tacitly supported by Sixtus IV involved the assassination of Lorenzo and Guiliano de Medici. Afterwards, several of its leaders like Archbishop Salviati were tossed out of tower windows by "the Eight."
swap.clue: Frederico Montelfeltro likely had a battalion waiting in the hills during this event, which left citizens hanging from the walls of the Palazzo Vecchio and tossed into the Arno river.

question.leadin: King Charles Robert I of this dynasty appears on the 200 Forint bill in Hungary, which he ruled from 1312 to 1342.
question.text: Name this royal house from the namesake area of France, who descend from a younger son of Blanche of Castile and more notably ruled Sicily and Naples.
question.clue: In 1460, Skanderbeg led an expedition to help Ferdinand I of Naples defend against this house. A member of this house, Charles II, defended against the House of Barcelona in the War of the Sicilian Vespers.

swap.text: Other bankers affiliated with P2 included this man, the chair of Banco Ambrosiano at the time of its collapse. His ties to the Vatican earned him the nickname "God's Banker."
